comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C5, C21, C28, C29, C38 regarding lysate experiments demonstrating sgRNA as the limiting factor for Cas9 activity. Both evaluations accept this mechanistic finding without reservation.

Disagreement on claims C6, C30, C31 regarding extended sgRNA versions. OpenEval finds insufficient quantitative data to verify enhancement claims, while peer reviewers acknowledge the improvement positively without requesting additional validation.

Perfect agreement on claims C35, C36, C37 regarding efficiency data. Both accept the 6-8% efficiency and comparison to ZFN/TALEN systems, with peer reviewers emphasizing that simplicity outweighs lower efficiency.

Strong agreement on core genome editing findings (C2, C3, C4, C18, C19, C20, C23, C27). Both evaluations affirm the demonstration of Cas9:sgRNA-mediated genome editing with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers describe work as 'excellent' and 'transformative.'

Strong agreement on claims C7, C43, C44 regarding main conclusions about RNA-guided genome editing as alternative to protein-based methods. Peer reviewers strongly endorse these conclusions, predicting the system will 'supplant ZFNs and TALE Nucleases.'

Both address sequencing validation (C55) of NHEJ-induced mutations. OpenEval finds the Surveyor assay and sequencing data provide robust evidence. Peer reviewers request sequencing confirmation, suggesting they accept the claim but want additional validation or clarification.

Both address Cas9 construct design and expression (C17 overlap). OpenEval focuses on experimental evidence for expression and localization. Peer reviewers affirm the overall capability demonstration, implicitly accepting these foundational results.

Partial overlap on C9 regarding off-target effects. OpenEval accepts background literature claims as appropriately cited. Peer reviewers raise uncertainty by requesting off-target analysis for the Cas9 system, questioning whether this limitation is adequately addressed.

OpenEval identifies claims C39, C40, C41, C42 about sgRNA stability and RNA modifications as speculative without experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic speculations.
OpenEval finds claims C45-C49 about multiplexing capability unsupported as they represent untested future directions. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these multiplexing proposals.

OpenEval accepts claim C54 regarding transfection efficiency data, noting standard methodology though suggesting additional rigor details would strengthen it. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval accepts claim C32 as appropriately qualified forward-looking statement about potential applications. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific discussion point.
